title: Cartier divisors, partial pullback, and rational sections on integral schemes
statement: Let $X$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-scheme] [def-pc-integral-scheme], with generic point $\eta$ [def-sc-generic-point] and function field $K(X)=\mathcal O_{X,\eta}$ [def-sc-function-field]. At $x$, the Cartier class of $f\in K(X)^\times$ is its coset $f\mathcal O_{X,x}^\times$ inside $K(X)$. A Cartier divisor is a function assigning such a class to every point, locally represented by one nonzero rational function. Equality is equality of all these classes. The zero divisor has equation $1$; support consists of points with nonunit class. For a scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$ between integral schemes, a divisor $E$ is the pullback of $D$ if at every $x$ there are $a,b\in\mathcal O_{Y,f(x)}$, with $a,b,f^\sharp a,f^\sharp b$ all nonzero, such that $a/b$ represents $D$ at $f(x)$ and $f^\sharp a/f^\sharp b$ represents $E$ at $x$. The canonical partial pullback returns that unique divisor when it exists uniquely, and is undefined otherwise. For an invertible module $L$ [def-sc-invertible-module], a rational section is an element of its generic stalk [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. It has Cartier divisor $D$ if at each $x$ a generator $t$ of $L_x$ has a nonzero rational coefficient $a$ with $s=a t_\eta$ and Cartier class $D_x$. It is an everywhere invertible regular section if it is the generic germ of a global regular section whose germ generates every stalk.
